value.rationale: A same-marginal, two-row SPD SOR coefficient-approximation problem is structurally motivated by mixed-precision splitting. The theorem proves a robust reversal between dependence choices: anticorrelation improves ordinary Gauss-Seidel yet fails at omega=187/100 where shared coupling succeeds, even though every sampled matrix is individually Schur stable. This is a substantive noncommuting random-product counterexample and separates single-sweep stability from second-moment stability. It is not a universal floating-point theorem and no practical speedup is asserted.
